As a young piano player and a 7th-grader, Toby has always been curious about the effects of music on people. He has done many tests on this. When he learned that people find it hard to focus, he wondered, "Could music help us improve attention?"
This 14-year-old boy started to search online for the effects of different kinds of music. He wanted to find out if listening to certain kinds of sounds could make people more focused. He then started an online test. He asked 65 people to play a computer game — they had to press a key when they saw certain numbers. Those people were divided into three groups. During the game, one group played in silence. Another group listened to a song from a video game. The third group heard a different tone (音调) in each ear, which created a special beating sound.
After the test, Toby compared the results. He found that the group with the special two-tone sound did the best. The group with the video game music did the worst. Although the results weren't strong enough to be completely sure, Toby didn't see that as a failure. For him, it was a starting point for more learning. "If you try something and it doesn't work, that's not a problem," he said. "It's part of the study process."
Later, Toby's project won him a prize in a national science contest. He hopes his work will help students discover new ways to focus when they study.

Vicky, a 14-year-old schoolgirl, was having difficulty with a piece of writing in English. She thought hard but achieved nothing, so she asked her teacher for some ideas to get started. In the end, she wrote one of her best pieces of work. She was really pleased that she had asked for help.
Everyone finds things difficult sometimes — Vicky is not the only one. Learning how to ask others to lend a hand is an important life skill.
When you might need help
There are lots of reasons why you could need help, such as having trouble with schoolwork or learning a new skill. When you're finding something difficult, or it's taking a long time to make progress, asking for help will move you forward more quickly than {{57}}.
What stops you asking for help
Asking for help isn't always easy. It can be tricky if you're not sure who to ask because you might think they won't want to help or they haven't got the time. If you think asking for a helping hand is a sign of weakness, it makes it even harder to turn to another person.
Asking for support is brave
Asking for help is an act of bravery. It takes great courage to let someone in, trust them with your story and ask them to help you deal with a problem.
When you ask for help, you won't face the pressure alone. As an old saying goes, “A problem shared is a problem halved.” There are other benefits too. By asking for help, you learn to express what you need. You can also put yourself in others' shoes and be more able to offer a helping hand when someone needs it.

Wonderful Christmas Gift

Christmas was so close, and so was Ann's birthday. She wished she could get a new dress with frills (荷叶边) and lace (蕾丝) as a wonderful Christmas gift. But Ann did not want to ask her mom for that. She knew how hard her mom worked to make a living. Maybe she could make a wish — maybe Santa Claus (圣诞老人) would come...
At school her classmates were talking only about Christmas celebrations. "My rich aunt is surely going to give me a pretty doll again." said Ria.
“I have been hinting (暗示) about that costly watch to my parents.” told Tessie.
Ann felt out of these conversations. She had neither rich parents nor wealthy aunts to give her expensive gifts.
It was not just the gift that worried Ann. It was her mother. Recently she was working overtime and looked pale and worn out.
Soon it was Christmas Eve. In everyone's house there was a decorated Christmas tree, but Ann's house was cold and empty. Every child went to bed eagerly waiting for the lovely gifts. Ann went to bed, wishing that at least this time she would get a gift from Santa Claus. Ann slowly drifted off to sleep. She dreamed of Santa riding in the snow...
The next morning, Ann jumped up after hearing her alarm. Out of her expectation, there lay a beautiful packet tied with a red ribbon near her bed. Inside the package was a pretty white dress with fluffy frills and attractive lace!
Ann checked the gift carefully to find out who had given her this beautiful dress. Suddenly a small piece of paper fell out from the dress.
Dear Ann, This dress is gifted to you for being a good girl. Hope you continue to do good things and help your mother.
Your Loving friend,
Santa Claus
Ann felt that there was something familiar about this note. She looked into the note carefully. Then it struck her. She realized that ___________________. Her mother had worked overtime to save money to buy this expensive gift. Ann was happy beyond words. She knew that she was the luckiest girl to have been given the best Christmas gift.

question_fact.material_text:
Vicky, a 14-year-old schoolgirl, was having difficulty with a piece of writing in English. She thought hard but achieved nothing, so she asked her teacher for some ideas to get started. In the end, she wrote one of her best pieces of work. She was really pleased that she had asked for help.
Everyone finds things difficult sometimes — Vicky is not the only one. Learning how to ask others to lend a hand is an important life skill.
When you might need help
There are lots of reasons why you could need help, such as having trouble with schoolwork or learning a new skill. When you're finding something difficult, or it's taking a long time to make progress, asking for help will move you forward more quickly than {{57}}.
What stops you asking for help
Asking for help isn't always easy. It can be tricky if you're not sure who to ask because you might think they won't want to help or they haven't got the time. If you think asking for a helping hand is a sign of weakness, it makes it even harder to turn to another person.
Asking for support is brave
Asking for help is an act of bravery. It takes great courage to let someone in, trust them with your story and ask them to help you deal with a problem.
When you ask for help, you won't face the pressure alone. As an old saying goes, “A problem shared is a problem halved.” There are other benefits too. By asking for help, you learn to express what you need. You can also put yourself in others' shoes and be more able to offer a helping hand when someone needs it.

Discovering the Power of Placebos (安慰剂)
A little girl cries after falling and bumping her knee against the ground. Her father rushes over and looks closely at the leg. "I'll kiss it and make it better," he says. The kiss works. The girl sniffles (抽噎), then jumps up and gets back to playing. Her pain is {{65}}.
Things like this one happen on playgrounds and in homes around the world every day. When a child gets a bump or bruise (淤伤), says Ulrike Bingel, "Someone will blow the pain away." Bingel is a doctor at a Germany university.
A caring adult seems to have the ability to stop a child's pain with a puff of air, a kiss or even just a few kind words. {{66}}, none of these things can repair injured skin. So what's happening? Doctors call it the placebo effect, it describes what happens when something that should have no effect leads to a(n) {{67}} positive change in someone's body.
Placebos are a very {{68}} part of medical research. To prove that a new medicine works, researchers must show that the people who are taking a new drug will be in much better health than those who are taking a placebo. This placebo is usually a pill and it {{69}} the same as the new medicine but contains no medicine. At times a person may feel better after taking a placebo pill though the pill did not act on any disease.
This placebo response isn't an illusion (幻觉). It comes from the brain. A placebo effect can only influence body processes that the brain can change like a pain. "Placebos can't fight cancer," Bingel says, "But they can change how {{70}} someone experiences pain or other illness."
Bingel and his team are working to better understand what brain processes make this happen.

The next morning, Ann jumped up after hearing her alarm. Out of her expectation, there lay a beautiful packet tied with a red ribbon near her bed. Inside the package was a pretty white dress with fluffy frills and attractive lace!
Ann checked the gift carefully to find out who had given her this beautiful dress. Suddenly a small piece of paper fell out from the dress.
Dear Ann, This dress is gifted to you for being a good girl. Hope you continue to do good things and help your mother.
Your Loving friend,
Santa Claus
Ann felt that there was something familiar about this note. She looked into the note carefully. Then it struck her. She realized that ___________________. Vicky, a 14-year-old schoolgirl, was having difficulty with a piece of writing in English. She thought hard but achieved nothing, so she asked her teacher for some ideas to get started. In the end, she wrote one of her best pieces of work. She was really pleased that she had asked for help.
Everyone finds things difficult sometimes — Vicky is not the only one. Learning how to ask others to lend a hand is an important life skill.
When you might need help
There are lots of reasons why you could need help, such as having trouble with schoolwork or learning a new skill. When you're finding something difficult, or it's taking a long time to make progress, asking for help will move you forward more quickly than {{57}}.
What stops you asking for help
Asking for help isn't always easy. It can be tricky if you're not sure who to ask because you might think they won't want to help or they haven't got the time. If you think asking for a helping hand is a sign of weakness, it makes it even harder to turn to another person.
Asking for support is brave
Asking for help is an act of bravery. It takes great courage to let someone in, trust them with your story and ask them to help you deal with a problem.
When you ask for help, you won't face the pressure alone. As an old saying goes, “A problem shared is a problem halved.” There are other benefits too. By asking for help, you learn to express what you need. You can also put yourself in others' shoes and be more able to offer a helping hand when someone needs it.

He then started an online test. He asked 65 people to play a computer game — they had to press a key when they saw certain numbers. Those people were divided into three groups. During the game, one group played in silence. Another group listened to a song from a video game. The third group heard a different tone (音调) in each ear, which created a special beating sound.
After the test, Toby compared the results. He found that the group with the special two-tone sound did the best. The group with the video game music did the worst. Although the results weren't strong enough to be completely sure, Toby didn't see that as a failure. For him, it was a starting point for more learning. question_facts.material_text:
Discovering the Power of Placebos (安慰剂)
A little girl cries after falling and bumping her knee against the ground. Her father rushes over and looks closely at the leg. "I'll kiss it and make it better," he says. The kiss works. The girl sniffles (抽噎), then jumps up and gets back to playing. Her pain is {{65}}.
Things like this one happen on playgrounds and in homes around the world every day. When a child gets a bump or bruise (淤伤), says Ulrike Bingel, "Someone will blow the pain away." Bingel is a doctor at a Germany university.
A caring adult seems to have the ability to stop a child's pain with a puff of air, a kiss or even just a few kind words. {{66}}, none of these things can repair injured skin. So what's happening? Doctors call it the placebo effect, it describes what happens when something that should have no effect leads to a(n) {{67}} positive change in someone's body.
Placebos are a very {{68}} part of medical research. To prove that a new medicine works, researchers must show that the people who are taking a new drug will be in much better health than those who are taking a placebo. This placebo is usually a pill and it {{69}} the same as the new medicine but contains no medicine. At times a person may feel better after taking a placebo pill though the pill did not act on any disease.
This placebo response isn't an illusion (幻觉). It comes from the brain. A placebo effect can only influence body processes that the brain can change like a pain. "Placebos can't fight cancer," Bingel says, "But they can change how {{70}} someone experiences pain or other illness."
Bingel and his team are working to better understand what brain processes make this happen.

The next morning, Ann jumped up after hearing her alarm. Out of her expectation, there lay a beautiful packet tied with a red ribbon near her bed. Inside the package was a pretty white dress with fluffy frills and attractive lace!
Ann checked the gift carefully to find out who had given her this beautiful dress. Suddenly a small piece of paper fell out from the dress.
Dear Ann, This dress is gifted to you for being a good girl. Hope you continue to do good things and help your mother.
Your Loving friend,
Santa Claus
Ann felt that there was something familiar about this note. She looked into the note carefully. Then it struck her. She realized that ___________________. As a young piano player and a 7th-grader, Toby has always been curious about the effects of music on people. He has done many tests on this. When he learned that people find it hard to focus, he wondered, "Could music help us improve attention?"
This 14-year-old boy started to search online for the effects of different kinds of music. He wanted to find out if listening to certain kinds of sounds could make people more focused. He then started an online test. He asked 65 people to play a computer game — they had to press a key when they saw certain numbers. Those people were divided into three groups. During the game, one group played in silence. Another group listened to a song from a video game. The third group heard a different tone (音调) in each ear, which created a special beating sound.
After the test, Toby compared the results. He found that the group with the special two-tone sound did the best. The group with the video game music did the worst. Although the results weren't strong enough to be completely sure, Toby didn't see that as a failure. For him, it was a starting point for more learning. "If you try something and it doesn't work, that's not a problem," he said. "It's part of the study process."
Later, Toby's project won him a prize in a national science contest. He hopes his work will help students discover new ways to focus when they study.

passages.material_text:
Vicky, a 14-year-old schoolgirl, was having difficulty with a piece of writing in English. She thought hard but achieved nothing, so she asked her teacher for some ideas to get started. In the end, she wrote one of her best pieces of work. She was really pleased that she had asked for help.
Everyone finds things difficult sometimes — Vicky is not the only one. Learning how to ask others to lend a hand is an important life skill.
When you might need help
There are lots of reasons why you could need help, such as having trouble with schoolwork or learning a new skill. When you're finding something difficult, or it's taking a long time to make progress, asking for help will move you forward more quickly than {{57}}.
What stops you asking for help
Asking for help isn't always easy. It can be tricky if you're not sure who to ask because you might think they won't want to help or they haven't got the time. If you think asking for a helping hand is a sign of weakness, it makes it even harder to turn to another person.
Asking for support is brave
Asking for help is an act of bravery. It takes great courage to let someone in, trust them with your story and ask them to help you deal with a problem.
When you ask for help, you won't face the pressure alone. As an old saying goes, “A problem shared is a problem halved.” There are other benefits too. By asking for help, you learn to express what you need. You can also put yourself in others' shoes and be more able to offer a helping hand when someone needs it.

Wonderful Christmas Gift

Christmas was so close, and so was Ann's birthday. She wished she could get a new dress with frills (荷叶边) and lace (蕾丝) as a wonderful Christmas gift. But Ann did not want to ask her mom for that. She knew how hard her mom worked to make a living. Maybe she could make a wish — maybe Santa Claus (圣诞老人) would come...
At school her classmates were talking only about Christmas celebrations. "My rich aunt is surely going to give me a pretty doll again." said Ria.
“I have been hinting (暗示) about that costly watch to my parents.” told Tessie.
Ann felt out of these conversations. She had neither rich parents nor wealthy aunts to give her expensive gifts.
It was not just the gift that worried Ann. It was her mother. Recently she was working overtime and looked pale and worn out.
Soon it was Christmas Eve. In everyone's house there was a decorated Christmas tree, but Ann's house was cold and empty. Every child went to bed eagerly waiting for the lovely gifts. Ann went to bed, wishing that at least this time she would get a gift from Santa Claus. Ann slowly drifted off to sleep. She dreamed of Santa riding in the snow...
The next morning, Ann jumped up after hearing her alarm. Out of her expectation, there lay a beautiful packet tied with a red ribbon near her bed. Inside the package was a pretty white dress with fluffy frills and attractive lace!
Ann checked the gift carefully to find out who had given her this beautiful dress. Suddenly a small piece of paper fell out from the dress.
Dear Ann, This dress is gifted to you for being a good girl. Hope you continue to do good things and help your mother.
Your Loving friend,
Santa Claus
Ann felt that there was something familiar about this note. She looked into the note carefully. Then it struck her. She realized that ___________________. Her mother had worked overtime to save money to buy this expensive gift. Ann was happy beyond words. She knew that she was the luckiest girl to have been given the best Christmas gift.

questions.question_text: When do people feel it harder to turn to others for help?
questions.correct_answer: When they think it is a sign of weakness.
questions.analysis: 这题更可能是你看到了前文“finding something difficult”这个熟悉表达，就直接拿来作答了，但题目真正问的不是“什么时候需要帮助”，而是“什么时候更难开口求助”。先看题干里的关键词“harder to turn to others for help”，再回到原文中找出现“harder”的句子，最后锁定真正的原因，是“把求助看成软弱的表现”。所以这题不是不会，而是定位到了相关话题，却没有落到最关键的那一句上。
questions.likely_thinking: 从答案看，较可能是你把“需要帮助的情境”和“更难去求助的原因”混在了一起。你先想到文章前面提到“当你觉得某件事很难时”，于是顺手写了那个内容，但没有继续往下核对题目问的是不是同一个层面。
questions.correct_thinking: 先读清题干，抓住核心问法是“什么时候会觉得更难向别人求助”；再回原文寻找与“harder”或“turn to another person”对应的句子；最后提取原因部分，也就是“if you think asking for a helping hand is a sign of weakness”。
questions.mistake: 核心错误是原文定位偏了，把“遇到困难”误当成了“更难开口求助的原因”。

m11.reading_strategy: 这类说明文通常会用小标题或分段来组织信息，所以先快速看每一段在讲“需要帮助”“不愿求助的原因”“求助的好处”中的哪一类。做题时不要只抓到同主题词就作答，还要核对题目问的是人物、原因、条件还是结果。遇到题干里的关键词，比如why, when, benefit, harder, because，要回原文找对应的逻辑词和原句。最后答题前用10秒复核：我写的答案，是否正好回答了题干的问题，而不是只和文章主题有关。

练习2：连续3天各做一篇任务型阅读，每做完专门检查一道错题：把题干中的关键词和原文对应句一一连线，再写一句“这题问的是___，不是___”。这个动作很适合改掉答偏的问题。
